text:
emma (sales): quick sync — enterprise lead wants a firm commit for H2 with a POC in 3 weeks. they estimate sustained 1800 qps at 256 tokens avg, 99th latency <200ms. asking which reserved GPU runway we should propose and what hedged capacity looks like
rajiv (solutions): 1800 qps sustained at 256 tokens is non-trivial. what model family? standard Llama2-70B or a quantized 4bit variant? both change GPU packing and KV-cache pressure
mike t. (infra): if they go with quantized 4bit we can target ~10k tokens/sec per A100-equivalent instance under our batching rules. rough calc: 1800 qps * 256 tokens = ~460k tokens/sec. that maps to ~46 A100-equivalent units raw. add 20% headroom -> 55 units. reserved pool recommendation: 56 GPUs for commit, with 12-16 burst credits for daily peaks
sofia (rev ops): pricing note — committing to 56 reserved GPUs for monthly commit moves them to dedicated pricing. should model both "soft-commit" (discounted, flexible) and "hard-commit" (SLA + deeper discount). soft-commit example: 30% discount, 2-week rolling notice. hard-commit: 45% discount, 3mo notice. need to show cost delta for POC -> production
chloe (security): also need to confirm data residency + encryption KMS for POC. dedicated instances can be VPC-only; we'll need the SOC docs updated in the security questionnaire before legal signs off
emma (sales): can we get a short runbook and a config snippet we can hand to the customer for the POC? they want autoscale + a fallback to smaller quantized model if tail latency spikes
capacity-bot: suggested autoscale policy generated on metrics: cpu_util, gpu_util, request_latency_99
rajiv (solutions): here's a minimal autoscale policy to start with — tweak thresholds after POC telemetry:

```
autoscale_policy:
  min_replicas: 48
  max_replicas: 72
  scale_up:
    metric: request_latency_99
    threshold_ms: 180
    step: +4
  scale_down:
    metric: gpu_util
    threshold_pct: 40
    step: -2
  fallback:
    model_variant: 4bit-optimized
    trigger_latency_ms: 250
```

rajiv (solutions): notes: min_replicas here maps to reserved capacity floor. fallback automates routing to 4bit variant when 99th >250ms for >15s
mike t. (infra): operational caveats: pre-warm KV cache for long context clients. if they have heavy prefix reuse we can cut required units by ~15%. also we need a canary that exercises worst-case seq length to validate kernel selection
sofia (rev ops): i'll draft the two pricing rows and spreadsheet. emma, can you ask the customer for 7-day qps histogram + percentiles? that will let us compute packing more accurately
chloe (security): addendum for questionnaire: "Are model parameters, prompts, and outputs logged? If so, where.\" answer: logs only keep metadata by default; payload logging disabled unless explicitly enabled and routed to customer-controlled S3 with SSE-KMS. include that in the doc
emma (sales): thanks — i'll collect histogram and push the security note. can we also show an example SLA fallback clause: if we miss 99th latency target for 3 consecutive days, we failover traffic to a lower-cost region or model variant
rajiv (solutions): suggest wording: "In event of persistent latency regression (99th >SLO for 3 consecutive days), Redwood will enable temporary routing to compatible model variants or secondary region and provide customers with detailed root cause and remediation plan."
mike t. (infra): one more: we should recommend a 10% buffer for autoscaling headroom during promo days. advise customer that reserved pool is baseline, and autoscaler burst uses burst credits charged at on-demand rates
emma (sales): perfect. i'll assemble POC packet (runbook, autoscale snippet, pricing rows, security Q answers) and share with the customer today. thanks team :thumbsup:
capacity-bot: policy saved to /policies/1778004321-hedged-provisioning.json
